source: McIntosh (2026) Linking generative AI and morphological analysis to conduct foresight evaluation, Foresight 28(1)
finding: Only paper found that puts an LLM directly on a Zwicky-style matrix. ChatGPT 4o judged which of 4 scenario views (columns) fit the real world, across 10 issues (rows) of a 1976 morphological field.
numbers: 4 views x 10 issues = 40 cells. Vertical pass (whole document): picked View B (Guarded Pessimist). Horizontal pass (new chat per issue, 4 unlabeled cells ranked 1-4, ranks summed): B 35/40 = 88%, A 27/40 = 68%, C 22/40 = 55%, D 16/40 = 40%. View B ranked best on 8 of 10 issues.
limits: One model, one date (7 Nov 2024), one prompt set, memory off. Reproducibility not tested. No ground truth, no quantitative indicators. Ranks are forced and relative. Model knowledge cutoff not disclosed in the answers. Possible negativity bias.
agent_relevance: Shows the cell-by-cell pattern: judge each matrix row in a fresh context, then sum with code. Fresh context per row and a second independent pass agreeing with the first is a cheap consistency check (G-style cross-check). Weak evidence, one pilot.

source: McIntosh (2026) same paper, method detail
finding: The two-pass design (holistic read, then per-row blind ranking with labels removed) gave the same winner. The author reports the one row where the rank order broke the pattern (Innovation and discovery, ambiguous wording).
numbers: Per-issue new conversation, 4 unlabeled write-ups, rank 4 = best fit, 1 = worst. Sum of ranks per view gives percent fit out of 40.
limits: Agreement between the two passes was not tested statistically. Labels removed to avoid label bias, but the model could still guess pessimism vs optimism from tone.
agent_relevance: Blinding cells (hide column labels) before judging is a bias guard that fits an S3 enumerate-then-judge step.

source: Park and Geum (2025) LLM-enhanced idea generation: data-driven morphological analysis with LDA and NuNER, Computers and Industrial Engineering
finding: Title and bibliographic record only (publisher page returned 403, Crossref has no abstract). It combines LDA topic modelling and the NuNER entity model to build the dimensions and values of a morphological matrix from text data, then uses an LLM to make ideas from combinations.
numbers: not read
limits: Not opened. Treat as a pointer: an LLM-era pipeline that builds the matrix from data instead of by hand.
agent_relevance: Worth a second pass by someone with access. The idea (extract dimensions and values from a corpus, enumerate by code, LLM writes each combination) is the S3 open-mode pattern.

source: Xiao, Zhang, McAdams (2026) Collaboration Between Two Large Language Models for Design Concept Generation, Journal of Mechanical Design
finding: Abstract only (via Crossref). A single LLM lacks diversity and novelty in design concepts. Three LLMs each wrote concepts for two engineering problems, then improved their own and the other two models' concepts. Two-LLM collaboration raised novelty and variety.
numbers: Three LLMs, two design problems. No effect sizes in the abstract.
limits: Abstract only. Not a morphological-chart study; relevant as a diversity fix.
agent_relevance: Cross-model recombination as a diversity source. For a single-agent scaffold, the analogue is a second pass that revises concepts from a different framing.

source: Si, Yang, Hashimoto (2024) Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas? A Large-Scale Human Study with 100+ NLP Researchers
finding: An over-generate-and-rank LLM agent produced ideas that expert reviewers rated more novel than human experts' ideas, but slightly weaker on feasibility.
numbers: Three conditions, N=49 ideas each. Novelty: human 4.84, AI 5.64, AI + human rerank 5.81 (AI vs human significant, p<0.01 in their table). 79 reviewers wrote 298 unique reviews.
limits: NLP prompting topics only. Reviewers are not outcome measures. Authors note follow-up execution study was needed.
agent_relevance: Large candidate pools plus a ranker beat unaided single ideas on novelty. This supports enumerate-then-select in S3.

source: Si et al. (2024) same paper, section 7.1 LLMs lack diversity
finding: Free over-generation saturates fast. Repeated sampling gives duplicates, so quantity does not give coverage.
numbers: 4000 seed ideas per topic, dedup at cosine 0.8 (all-MiniLM-L6-v2): only about 200 non-duplicates remain (about 5%). Non-duplicate share of each new batch keeps falling, accumulated unique count plateaus.
limits: Threshold 0.8 chosen by manual inspection. Embedding similarity may merge ideas a human sees as different.
agent_relevance: Core argument for a matrix: sampling the same prompt many times does not span the space. Forcing coverage by code over dimension values is the fix a Zwicky box offers.

source: Si et al. (2024) same paper, LLM-as-judge results
finding: LLM judges are poor at ranking ideas against human review scores. Pairwise ranking from the authors was better than direct scoring but still weak.
numbers: Balanced top/bottom-25% idea ranking task, accuracy: GPT-4o direct 50.0, GPT-4o pairwise 45.0, Claude-3.5 direct 51.7, AI Scientist reviewer 43.3, authors' ranker 56.1 (chance 50). Inter-human consistency in same table is higher (see paper).
limits: Ranking target is mean reviewer score, which is noisy. Numbers read from a flattened PDF table; column alignment checked only roughly.
agent_relevance: Do not let the model pick the best cell of a matrix on its own judgment alone. Use external checks, cheap tests, or multiple blind comparisons (G-style guardrail on self-grading).

source: Meincke, Mollick, Terwiesch (2024) Prompting Diverse Ideas: Increasing AI Idea Variance (Wharton working paper)
finding: GPT-4 idea pools are less diverse than human group pools. Prompt engineering narrows the gap; chain-of-thought (list, then make bold and different, then describe) was among the best.
numbers: 35 prompts, 10 sessions x 100 ideas each, product ideas for college students under $50. Mean cosine similarity: human groups 0.243; GPT-4 pools 0.255 to 0.432. Baseline 0.377. Steve Jobs persona 0.368. HBR creativity-tools prompt 0.387. CoT raised unique-idea count from about 3700 (base prompt) to 4700.
limits: One domain, one model (GPT-4, 2023). Cosine on embeddings is a proxy. Unique-count is extrapolated.
agent_relevance: Name-the-technique prompts (HBR creativity tools) barely helped, while a multi-step structure did. A matrix is multi-step structure forced by code, so it should be at least as strong; no direct test found.

source: Meincke, Mollick, Terwiesch (2024) same paper, speed of exhaustion
finding: The paper also tracks how fast the idea space is used up, and that listing prompts differ in how quickly new unique ideas stop arriving.
numbers: Hybrid brainstorming pool combines ideas from 40 GPT-4 sessions, picking and refining the best 4 at a time. Similarity-information prompt told GPT-4 the cosine of existing ideas.
limits: Exact exhaustion curves not extracted in this session.
agent_relevance: Telling the model what has already been covered is a prompt-level stand-in for a matrix coverage map. Code can do this exactly: mark visited cells.

source: Doshi and Hauser (2024) Generative AI enhances creativity but reduces the diversity of novel content, Science Advances
finding: Human writers given AI story ideas wrote better-rated stories, but stories across writers became more alike.
numbers: 293 writers, 600 evaluators, 3 conditions (none, 1 AI idea, up to 5 AI ideas). Novelty +6.7% (b=0.259, p=0.001) vs human-only mean 3.85; 5 ideas +8.1%; usefulness +9.0% with 5 ideas. Low-creativity writers gained up to 10.7% novelty. Stories 5.2% more similar to the AI idea they saw (b=4.29, p<0.001, human-only mean 82.85).
limits: Short 8-sentence stories, one GPT-4 idea source, online sample.
agent_relevance: AI-seeded ideas anchor the user and homogenise the pool. Anchoring on the first idea is what a matrix is meant to prevent, by presenting all value options side by side.

source: Zhang et al. (2025) Verbalized Sampling: How to Mitigate Mode Collapse and Unlock LLM Diversity
finding: Asking the model for several responses with their probabilities in one prompt restores diversity lost by alignment, with no training.
numbers: Creative writing diversity 1.6-2.1x over direct prompting; human evaluation +25.7%; recovers 66.8% of base-model diversity. More capable models gain more. Quality and factual accuracy not hurt per authors.
limits: Tasks are poems, stories, jokes, dialogue simulation, QA. Not design concepts.
agent_relevance: A cheaper alternative to a full matrix when dimensions are unknown: one structured prompt that lists a distribution. Could seed the dimension-value lists in S3.

source: Jiang et al. (2025) Artificial Hivemind: The Open-Ended Homogeneity of Language Models
finding: Many models give very similar answers to open-ended prompts, so asking several models does not fix coverage.
numbers: Infinity-Chat: 26K real open-ended queries, 31,250 human annotations. Average pairwise similarity of responses to the same prompt exceeds 0.8 in 79% of cases. With min-p decoding 61.2% of response pairs still exceed 0.8. Cross-model similarity 71% to 82%; DeepSeek-V3 vs qwen-max 0.82.
limits: Embedding similarity; 'open-ended' judged by LLM and annotators.
agent_relevance: Temperature and model ensembles are weak diversity levers. Structural levers (forced dimension values chosen by code) are not subject to the same collapse, though the cell content written by the model still can be.

source: Yu et al. (2023) Large Language Model as Attributed Training Data Generator: A Tale of Diversity and Bias (AttrPrompt), NeurIPS Datasets and Benchmarks
finding: Closest published analogue to a morphological matrix run by code: attribute dimensions (e.g. length, style, location) with values, combined into prompts. Beat plain class-conditional prompts.
numbers: Matches simple-prompt performance with 5% of ChatGPT query cost. Simple prompts biased: NYT location attribute 68.01% North America vs 0.69% Africa. Fixing one attribute dimension to its best value and randomising the rest lowered downstream accuracy; composing all best values into one config was significantly worse than random configs.
limits: Text classification data generation, not design. Enumerating all combinations was too costly, so random sampling of configurations was used, not full cross-product.
agent_relevance: Strong support: attribute-dimension sampling raises diversity and cuts bias. Also shows picking each dimension's 'best' value separately is a trap (combination effects), the known weakness of un-checked morphological selection.

source: Yu et al. (2023) same paper, how attributes were built
finding: An LLM (ChatGPT) was used to propose the attribute dimensions and the values, with human review; prompts then combined values randomly.
numbers: Class-dependent attributes sampled one value per class and repeated 5 times because enumerating all combinations was too expensive.
limits: Dimension quality depends on the LLM's proposal; no ablation of poor dimension choice found in the text read.
agent_relevance: Matches the step 'LLM proposes the parameters and values, code does the cross product'. Combinatorial explosion forces sampling or pruning.

source: Radensky et al. (2026) Scideator: Human-LLM Compound System for Scientific Ideation through Facet Recombination and Novelty Evaluation, ACM CAIS 26
finding: A matrix-like system: ideas split into facets (purpose, mechanism, evaluation), facets from retrieved papers recombined by the LLM, novelty checked against literature.
numbers: User study, 22 CS researchers (16 PhD students), within-subject vs baseline with the same LLM and no facet modules. Creativity Support Index median 70.5 vs 61.0 (Wilcoxon p<.01); gains in exploration and expressiveness.
limits: Small N, CSI is self-report. Participants noted tool ideas could still be a synthesis rather than beyond input papers.
agent_relevance: Structured facet interaction beat free-text prompting on the same model. Evidence for putting a table, not prose, between the model and the user in S3.

source: Radensky et al. (2026) same paper, novelty classifier ablation
finding: Judging novelty facet by facet with expert-labelled examples was much more accurate than prompts that reason over unstructured ideas.
numbers: Accuracy / macro F1: expert in-context facet classifier 0.78 / 0.77; zero-shot 0.68 / 0.65; OpenReview in-context examples 0.59 / 0.43; AI Scientist novelty prompt 0.47 / 0.44.
limits: Small labelled set (51 ideas assessed by the first two authors for one analysis). Domain NLP/HCI.
agent_relevance: Per-dimension comparison (is this cell new on dimension X?) works better than a single holistic 'is it novel?'. Use per-dimension checks.

source: Egea et al. (2025) ChatGPT as an inventor: eliciting the strengths and weaknesses of current LLMs against humans in engineering design, AI EDAM
finding: In a 48-hour prototyping hackathon with 100+ prototypes, ChatGPT 4.0 directing two participants finished second of six teams. Concept generation was strong but it showed design fixation and dropped promising concepts early.
numbers: 6 teams, LLM team second. It produced many working principles (slingshot, gravity, centrifugal) but built only 3 recurring concepts. One concept (pneumatics) abandoned after one iteration due to a valve fit problem.
limits: One hackathon, one LLM version, single LLM team so no variance estimate. Participants acted as the LLM's hands.
agent_relevance: The model lists many options but then converges on the safe few. A matrix with an explicit selection rule (code) and a rule to keep a runner-up alive counters this.

source: Egea et al. (2025) same paper, key finding 9 on fixation
finding: The LLM fixated on details in the prompt, such as the last item in a list of available machines.
numbers: Qualitative observation during pilot prompts; no frequency given.
limits: Anecdotal, no counts.
agent_relevance: Order effect inside lists: when options are written as a list the model may favour the last. Shuffle option order across runs when enumerating matrix values.

source: Egea et al. (2025) same paper, recommendations
finding: Authors recommend explicitly prompting the LLM to consider alternatives to avoid fixation, plus human oversight, feedback loops and subsystem-level tasks.
numbers: Six recommendations in total; no tested effect size for the alternatives prompt.
limits: Recommendations not experimentally tested.
agent_relevance: The subsystem-level advice is the same decomposition a morphological chart makes (function by function). Untested here, so a hypothesis for our own bench.

source: Jiang and Luo (2024) AutoTRIZ: Automating Engineering Innovation with TRIZ and LLMs
finding: An LLM pipeline runs a fixed multi-step method (contradiction, parameters, principles, solution report). The abstract names morphological analysis as a method that could be automated the same way.
numbers: 10 textbook cases from 7 books, each run 100 times; entropy of contradiction detection from 0 to 6.64; in 7 of 10 cases the textbook answer matched or half-matched within the top 3 detections. Case study battery thermal management: +20-30% grouping efficiency and volumetric energy density, more than +60% thermal management efficiency vs best existing scheme, by their model.
limits: Textbook answer is not a gold standard (authors say). Case study metrics come from authors' own simulation model.
agent_relevance: Same LLM-plus-method-skeleton design a morphological scaffold would use. Self-consistency over 100 runs shows high-entropy steps (here, which parameter) are where the model is unreliable; use votes there.

source: Jiang and Luo (2024) AutoTRIZ, section 4.2 consistency
finding: Higher-probability outputs matched the textbook better, in every case. In most cases one parameter stayed fixed while the other varied across runs.
numbers: Cases 5, 6, 7, 8 had a dominant top-1 detection. Entropy upper bound 6.64 for 100 runs.
limits: Only 10 cases, authors say too few for significance.
agent_relevance: Modal answer across runs is a usable confidence signal for choosing which cell/parameter to fix first.

source: Alvander, Lunden, Gavel (2009) A computerized optimization framework for the morphological matrix applied to aircraft conceptual design, Computer-Aided Design
finding: Older computational system: the morphological matrix is searched with optimisation software against performance calculations (record only, no abstract available from Crossref).
numbers: not read
limits: Not opened. Aircraft conceptual design case.
agent_relevance: Prior art for 'code enumerates, a model scores': combinations are evaluated by a calculator rather than by taste. Check the full text before relying on it.

source: Ritchey (2006) Problem structuring using computer-aided morphological analysis, Journal of the Operational Research Society 57(7)
finding: Older AI-style tool: general morphological analysis software with a cross-consistency assessment that removes impossible value pairs, shrinking the solution space (record only, no abstract fetched).
numbers: not read
limits: Not opened; description from title and citation record only.
agent_relevance: The consistency matrix (pairwise compatibility of values) is exactly the part an LLM can fill cheaply and code can apply as a filter. Worth reading in full.

source: Filippi (2023) Measuring the Impact of ChatGPT on Fostering Concept Generation in Innovative Product Design, Electronics 12(16):3535
finding: Abstract only. Compares ChatGPT-supported concept generation against 'classic' design methods using metrics on participants' concepts; provides an Excel workbook for analysis.
numbers: not read (publisher page returned 403).
limits: Not opened; method list unknown, may not include morphological charts.
agent_relevance: A candidate for the human-vs-ChatGPT concept metrics (quantity, variety, novelty) borrowed from Shah's ideation effectiveness. Needs full-text check.

source: Nomaguchi et al. (2025) Creating design catalog from patent documents with LLM for design concept generation, Proc. Design Society
finding: Abstract only. LLM extracts problem-solution pairs from patents as purpose-means pairs, clusters them into a design catalog, then new concepts are generated from the catalog (martial arts devices case).
numbers: no quantitative result in the abstract.
limits: Case study; effectiveness 'demonstrated', not measured.
agent_relevance: A design catalog is a machine-built morphological table of means per function. Shows LLMs can fill the value lists from a corpus.

source: Ren, Ma, Luo (2025) Large language model for patent concept generation, Advanced Engineering Informatics 65:103301
finding: Negative check: the paper fine-tunes an LLM on patents (knowledge injection pretraining, SFT, RLHF) for concept and patent generation. It does not use a morphological chart; no morphological-analysis content found in its text.
numbers: Reported as outperforming state of the art on patent benchmarks; exact figures not extracted.
limits: Not a test of this subfield. Included to mark that grep of the full text for 'morpholog' returned nothing.
agent_relevance: Training-based; outside our no-training scope.

source: Ch'ng (2025) Human-AI Co-Ideation in VR Experience Design: Evaluating the Dimensionality Framework (8Df) with LLMs, Research Square preprint
finding: Abstract only. A fixed 8-dimension framework (spatial, sensory, placeness, temporal, cultural, social, cognitive, psychological) structured co-ideation with ChatGPT, Gemini and DeepSeek. Models differed in style: ChatGPT preset-to-prototype, Gemini facilitator, DeepSeek classification and blended.
numbers: qualitative; no numbers in abstract.
limits: Preprint, qualitative, 3 models.
agent_relevance: Dimension-structured prompts change model behaviour per model; a matrix scaffold may need per-model tuning.

source: Search coverage note (this session)
finding: Searches of arXiv, Semantic Scholar and Crossref (web search budget was exhausted; arXiv and Semantic Scholar APIs rate limited) found no controlled study that compares an LLM with and without a Zwicky morphological box on idea quality or coverage. Closest direct tests are the foresight pilot (c01) and facet/attribute recombination systems (c13, c15).
numbers: 0 direct randomized comparisons found; 1 direct LLM-on-matrix pilot (c01).
limits: Search was thin: no OpenAlex, no Google Scholar. Absence is not proof. Park and Geum 2025 (c03) may be a direct test.
agent_relevance: Our matrix scaffold is untested by the literature; treat as a hypothesis to bench in our harness, with enumeration-by-code vs plain sampling as the contrast, scored by dedup count at cosine 0.8 as in c06.
